_comment: @sievan/design is a private GitHub repo consumed as an npm git dependency.
npm records it in package-lock.json as an ssh URL no matter how package.json
spells it, and a Vercel build container has no SSH key, so the install fails
there and only there. This rewrites that URL to https with a token.
--add is load-bearing: all three rewrites share one config key, and without
it each call replaces the previous one, leaving only the last. npm asks for
the ssh:// form, which would be the one silently dropped.
Set SIEVAN_DESIGN_TOKEN in the Vercel project: a fine-grained PAT with
read-only Contents on lalaf02/sievan-design and nothing else. The guard means
a checkout without the variable still installs normally.
npm install rather than npm ci: ci refuses outright when package.json and
the lockfile disagree on how this URL is spelled, which it did, and which
fails before the fetch is even attempted. install is also Vercel's own
default, so this changes only the credential, not the build.
If sievan-design is ever made public, delete this file — the dependency then
resolves anonymously and no token is needed.
installCommand: if [ -n "$SIEVAN_DESIGN_TOKEN" ]; then R="https://x-access-token:$SIEVAN_DESIGN_TOKEN@github.com/"; git config --global --add url."$R".insteadOf ssh://git@github.com/; git config --global --add url."$R".insteadOf git@github.com:; git config --global --add url."$R".insteadOf https://github.com/; fi; npm install
